transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start off, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

Hi. Thank you. Um... well, I think what finally brought me in is that I just feel like the part of me that used to reach out for people has gone very quiet. 

I used to take a lot of pleasure in things—my work, doing yoga, going to art galleries, even just journaling at home. But lately... I don't know, it's like that spark is missing. I'm mostly just moving through my daily obligations right now without really feeling much of anything about them.
How long has this loss of interest and low mood been going on—days, weeks, or longer?

It's been longer than a few weeks. Um... I'd say this whole change in how I'm thinking, working, and just connecting with people... it's been going on for about eight months now. It really started right around the time we took an older relative into our apartment to live with us.
Have you ever had a period—lasting several days or more—when you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than usual, even if it felt good at the time?

No, I haven't. I've never really had a time like that. I've always been pretty even-keeled... or, well, at least until recently, when I just started feeling so flat. But no, I haven't had any periods where I felt super energetic or didn't need sleep.
Have you ever experienced a similar period of low mood and loss of interest like this at any other time in your life, before these last eight months?

No, I haven't. Um... this is really the first time I've ever felt this way. I've always been pretty steady throughout my life, you know, before all this started. So, no, nothing like this before the last eight months.
Despite feeling this way, are you still able to keep up with your work and daily responsibilities, or has it become difficult to manage them?

It's definitely become difficult. I mean, I’m still showing up to work, but... I'm just not functioning at my usual level. I've actually missed a couple of grant deadlines recently. And my supervisor has noticed, I think. She’s quietly moved some of my more demanding clients to other clinicians. So, I'm there, but I'm really struggling to actually keep up with my responsibilities.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or that life isn't worth living during this time?
No, no thoughts like that. I haven't wanted to hurt myself or anything. I just feel... empty, I guess, but not like I want to end things.
Beyond work, how are you managing with everyday things like taking care of yourself, household responsibilities, or spending time with family and friends?

I'm getting by, I guess, but it's... it's hard. I'm still doing the basics, like showering and eating, but the chores are definitely piling up at home. I just don't have the energy to do laundry or clean right now. 

And as for friends and family... I've mostly just been keeping to myself. I haven't really felt up to socializing or reaching out to anyone. I mostly just come home from work and stay in.
Have you been feeling unusually worthless or excessively guilty about things, even minor issues, during this time?

No, not really. I mean, I know I'm dropping the ball at work right now, but I don't feel worthless or... overly guilty about it. I just don't have the drive I usually do. So, no, I haven't been having those kinds of thoughts.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to concentrate or make decisions, or any slowing down (or restlessness) in how you move or think?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. My concentration seems fine, and I don't feel like I'm moving slower or feeling restless or anything. It's really just the lack of energy and motivation I mentioned before.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns or appetite since this started—such as sleeping much more or less than usual, or a significant change in your appetite or weight?

No, my sleep has been pretty normal. I'm getting my usual seven or eight hours a night. And my appetite is about the same, too. I haven't noticed any weight gain or loss... I'm just eating what I normally eat. So, no changes there.

No manic/hypomanic history (ruling out bipolar disorder), no prior depressive episodes (first episode), no psychotic features, no suicidal ideation, and no vegetative symptoms (sleep/appetite normal), no psychomotor changes, no guilt/worthlessness, and concentration intact. This yields roughly 4 core symptoms (depressed mood, anhedonia, fatigue, functional impairment) meeting criteria for a single moderate depressive episode (F32.1) rather than mild (fewer symptoms/impairment) or severe (no significant additional symptoms like guilt, psychomotor changes, or suicidality). The onset coincided with a stressor (relative moving in), but the pervasive, sustained nature of symptoms across all domains (work, home, social) for 8 months exceeds typical adjustment disorder duration/severity, favoring a major depressive episode diagnosis.
